# 2013A Question 15 (old) {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the peripheral and central nervous system pathways that lead to the perception of pain following a laceration to the thumb.
:::

Also asked in: [2021A Question 5](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/5/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the pathway from transduction in the thumb through peripheral afferents, spinal processing and ascending pathways to cortical perception. Use a labelled pathway diagram and include emotional, autonomic and descending modulatory components.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Nociceptors and Transduction

### Peripheral Afferents and Spinal Entry

### Dorsal Horn Synapses and Processing

### Ascending and Supraspinal Pathways

### Cortical, Emotional and Autonomic Processing

### Descending Modulation
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
Old Exam: **40%** of candidates achieved a pass in this question

It was possible to achieve almost full marks for this question with a simple well labelled diagram. Those candidates who did not perform well in this question invariably did so as a result of not imparting basic facts. This topic is well covered in the physiology textbooks on the reading list, and as such a model answer will not be repeated here.
:::
